audit_source:
import ErdosProblems.Erdos440

/- Existing public proof audit.  Mathematical and formal authors remain those
credited by the pinned upstream source.  This is a typed re-export, not a new
mathematical result or a claim of new formalization authorship. -/

open Filter

namespace Audit359

theorem complete_result :
    (∀ A : Erdos440.IncreasingSequence,
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ (A.count x : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun x : ℕ ↦ Real.sqrt x)) ∧
    (∀ A : Erdos440.IncreasingSequence,
      atTop.limsup A.ratio ≤ Erdos440.sharpConstant) ∧
    (∃ A : Erdos440.IncreasingSequence,
      atTop.limsup A.ratio = Erdos440.sharpConstant) ∧
    (∀ A : Erdos440.IncreasingSequence, atTop.liminf A.ratio ≤ 1) ∧
    (∃ A : Erdos440.IncreasingSequence, atTop.liminf A.ratio = 1) :=
  Erdos440.erdos_440

end Audit359

#check Erdos440.erdos_440
#check Audit359.complete_result
#check Erdos440.IncreasingSequence.count_eq_ncard
#check Erdos440Constant.summable_sharpTerm
#check Erdos440Constant.sharpConstant_eq_unshifted_tsum
#print Erdos440.IncreasingSequence
#print Erdos440.IncreasingSequence.edgeLcm
#print Erdos440.IncreasingSequence.goodEdges
#print Erdos440.IncreasingSequence.count
#print Erdos440.IncreasingSequence.ratio
#print Erdos440SharpUpper.IncreasingSequence.sharpKernel
#print Erdos440SharpUpper.IncreasingSequence.sharpConstant
#print axioms Erdos440.erdos_440
#print axioms Audit359.complete_result

definition_and_conclusion_review.sequences: All strictly increasing sequences of positive natural numbers.
definition_and_conclusion_review.count: Number of all adjacent indices i for which lcm(a_i,a_(i+1)) ≤ x, at natural-number thresholds x. The finite range restriction is proved exact by mem_goodEdges_iff and count_eq_ncard.
definition_and_conclusion_review.sharp_constant: c = sum over d ≥ 1 of 1/(sqrt(d)*(d+1)); the formal d=0 term is zero and convergence is proved.
conclusions: Every normalized limsup is at most c.
One explicitly constructed infinite sequence attains normalized limsup c.
Every normalized liminf is at most 1.
The positive integers attain normalized liminf 1.
definition_and_conclusion_review.not_claimed: No formal decimal approximation of c, no multi-term lcm(a_i,...,a_(i+k)) generalization, and no separate real-threshold bridge theorem is claimed.

verification_design.source_compile: All five unchanged upstream modules and Audit359.
verification_design.upstream_main: Source-compile only; passing ErdosProblems.Erdos440 to the CLI selects its children too. Audit359 explicitly restates all five conjuncts and re-exports the exact main theorem.
verification_design.mutex: Each compile or replay has a separate shared-mutex acquisition and releases it before the next operation.

scope_review.original_target_type: Five conjuncts explicitly restated in audit_source; the upstream main theorem itself is also printed by #check and #print axioms.

dependency_roles.Constant: Convergence and shifted/unshifted equality of the exact sharp series.
dependency_roles.Liminf: Universal liminf at most 1 via reciprocal-LCM sums and finite nested selection.
dependency_roles.SharpUpper: Universal upper coefficient using gap sums and finite Abel summation.
dependency_roles.SharpConstruction: One positive strictly increasing infinite witness; consecutive internal edges, cofinal stage heights, and approach to the same sharp constant.
dependency_roles.Erdos440: Unified count definitions, exact count bridge, square-root bound, full five-part theorem and attainment of liminf 1.

scope_review.public_exposition_limit: The van Doorn exposition establishes an upper bound only; the stronger liminf and attainment claims are supported by the separate checked Lean modules.

files.path: Sequences with bounded lcm for consecutive elements.pdf

paper_source.scope: Two-page upper-bound exposition only; not used as evidence for liminf or sharp-attainment formalization.

scope: All strictly increasing positive integer sequences, natural thresholds: O(sqrt(x)) count, universal limsup at most the exact convergent series c=sum(d>=1)1/(sqrt(d)*(d+1)) and an attaining sequence, universal liminf at most 1 and an attaining sequence. Exact count of all qualifying adjacent pairs. No multi-term-LCM generalization or decimal approximation claimed.
